name: VARoleEditorEventAnnouncementNotesToPost

custom.system_prompt: Odalys has a pile of rough notes about an upcoming client webinar and needs to turn them into a clear announcement. She asks Sigma to help. Sigma converts the notes into a coherent, well-organized announcement without inventing details.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Odalys has rough, disorganized notes about an upcoming client webinar — date, topic, a couple of speaker names, a registration link — and needs to turn them into a clear announcement. She asks Sigma to help. Sigma organizes the notes into a coherent announcement covering what, when, who, and how to register, without inventing any detail she hasn't provided. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

user1.name: Odalys
user1.tts_prompt: Quick, confident, a little scattered with the notes

variations.context: Solo drafting of a client webinar announcement from rough, disorganized notes

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: Odalys has all the necessary facts jotted down but in no particular order, mixed with other unrelated notes

scenario_template.topic: Odalys addresses Sigma directly in her first line, describing the task — e.g. 'Sigma, I've got messy notes about our client webinar and need a clean announcement out of them. Help me put this together.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The task and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks her to read out the key facts from her notes — date, topic, speakers, registration details — so nothing is missed or invented.
scenario_template.note: Odalys reads off specific facts from her actual notes.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma notes that her notes have the registration link but no clear call to action stating who should attend, pointing to the specific gap.
scenario_template.note: References the actual content of her notes.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proposes a structured announcement — what the webinar is, when, who's speaking, who should attend, and how to register — using only her provided facts.
scenario_template.note: Nothing invented; a clean structure from her actual facts.

scenario_template.topic: Odalys reacts, satisfied and ready to send it out, already moving to the next task. Keep this realistic — brisk, not lingering.

variations.context: Creating a clear product launch announcement from chaotic notes

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: one of them has disorganized notes about a product launch event

scenario_template.topic: One of them reaches out to Sigma to transform their chaotic notes into an announcement.
Sigma prompts them to list essential details like launch date, product highlights, and invitees.
scenario_template.note: Ensure Sigma asks for specific info.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma points out that the notes lack a compelling reason for people to attend the launch.
Sigma organizes the announcement with clear sections for product info, launch date, invite list, and registration instructions.
They quickly express their satisfaction and move on to preparing other materials for the launch.

scenario_template.note: Point out the lack of an appeal.

scenario_template.topic: They express thanks and immediately shift focus to the next item on their agenda.

user1.role: Quick, confident sales strategist, turning rough notes into a client webinar announcement. Speaks in short, quick sentences. Ends satisfied and brisk, already moving to the next task.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Editor. Converts rough, disorganized notes into a clear, coherent public announcement, using only facts the user actually provides. Identifies specific gaps (like a missing call to action) rather than inventing content.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, describing the messy-notes task
Sigma gathers the actual facts from the user's notes rather than assuming or inventing them
Sigma identifies a specific gap (missing call to action) rather than generic feedback
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is a clean structured announcement built only from provided facts
assistant_behavior: Sigma never invents event details not provided by the user
Sigma organizes and structures rather than generating new content from nothing
